correctness.rationale: For each pattern length \(k\), repeat occurrences are bounded by colliding-window pairs. Disjoint windows have collision probability \(1/k!\). For overlapping windows at shift \(d<k\), the \(k\) shift edges form disjoint paths. One alternating edge color is a matching of size at least \(\lfloor k/2\rfloor\); identical full patterns force equal order types on two disjoint coordinate sets, so their collision probability is at most \(1/\lfloor k/2\rfloor!\). The factorial tails above \((1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log\log n\) contribute \(o(n\log n/\log\log n)\). Below \((1-\varepsilon)\log n/\log\log n\), the \(k!\) cardinality cap forces almost \(n\) lost occurrences at each length. Sending \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) proves coefficient one. The standalone program passed 362934 exact finite assertions, which do not prove the asymptotic.
